newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish bank BOS sees 1996 net rising of PLN 54 mln.
newsitem.headline: Polish bank BOS sees 1996 net rising of PLN 54 mln.

text.p: Polish bank Bank Ochrony Srodowiska SA (BOS) whose public offering starts later this month, expects its net profit to rise this year to 54 million zlotys from 31.8 million in 1995, the bank's president said.
"We expect to make 54 million zlotys this year...and if there's a variation it shouldn't be significant," Jozef Koziol told a news conference on Tuesday.
In a report released on Tuesday the brokerage unit of Bank Handlowy SA predicted BOS would net 46.6 million zlotys.
BOS plans to enter the Warsaw bourse's main market in January.

Koziol said his earnings estimation assumed that all of the 1.2 million shares on offer would be taken up at the maximum price of 29 zlotys under which investors currently could make offers through book building. The minimum price is 23 zlotys.
BOS financial adviser Grzegorz Medza said the final price would be announced not later than two days before the start of the subscription on October 21.
Large investors can subscribe for at least 25,000 shares in the large-investor tranche of 800,000 shares from October 21 to 25. The retail tranche of 400,000 shares is due between October 21 and 31.
Medza said about three quarters of the proceeds would go toward increasing lending for environmental projects with much of the rest going toward upgrading the bank's computer system.
The issue will be valid if investors subscribe for 600,000 shares, and Medza said an underwriter could still be chosen by Friday if it were not certain all the shares would be taken.
Koziol said BOS would pay a 1996 dividend of up to 40 percent of 1996 earnings, with the new shareholders included.

The bank's main shareholders are the National Fund for Environmental Protection and Water Management, with 44.4 percent, the State Treasury, with 7.7 percent, and state-controlled chemical trader Ciech SA with 5.8 percent.
Koziol also said he expected total environmental spending in Poland from 1994 to 2000 to amount to 21.9 billion zlotys.
